From Lemma A.7 we have

VarP⁡(V)=(1−τ)​Varhead+τ​Vartail+τ⁡(1−τ)​‖μtail−μhead‖22≥τ⁡(1−τ)​‖μtail−μhead‖22.\operatorname{Var}_{P}(V)=(1-\tau)\operatorname{Var}_{\mathrm{head}}+\tau\operatorname{Var}_{\mathrm{tail}}+\tau(1-\tau)\,\|\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}-\mu_{\mathrm{head}}\|_{2}^{2}\;\geq\;\tau(1-\tau)\,\|\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}-\mu_{\mathrm{head}}\|_{2}^{2}.

Hence

‖μtail−μhead‖22≤VarP⁡(V)τ⁡(1−τ).\|\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}-\mu_{\mathrm{head}}\|_{2}^{2}\;\leq\;\frac{\operatorname{Var}_{P}(V)}{\tau(1-\tau)}.

Multiplying both sides by τ2\tau^{2} and taking square roots gives

τ​‖μtail−μhead‖2≤τ1−τ​VarP⁡(V).\tau\,\|\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}-\mu_{\mathrm{head}}\|_{2}\;\leq\;\sqrt{\frac{\tau}{1-\tau}}\,\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_{P}(V)}.

It remains to compute Dχ2(P^∥P)D_{\chi^{2}}(\hat{P}\|P) for Top-kk. By definition,

Dχ2(P^∥P)=∑i=1n(p^i−pi)2pi.D_{\chi^{2}}(\hat{P}\|P)=\sum_{i=1}^{n}\frac{(\hat{p}_{i}-p_{i})^{2}}{p_{i}}.

For i≤ki\leq k, p^i=pi/(1−τ)\hat{p}_{i}=p_{i}/(1-\tau), so

(p^i−pi)2pi=pi​(11−τ−1)2=pi​(τ1−τ)2.\frac{(\hat{p}_{i}-p_{i})^{2}}{p_{i}}=p_{i}\Bigl(\frac{1}{1-\tau}-1\Bigr)^{2}=p_{i}\Bigl(\frac{\tau}{1-\tau}\Bigr)^{2}.

Summing over i≤ki\leq k yields

∑i≤k(p^i−pi)2pi=(τ1−τ)2​∑i≤kpi=(τ1−τ)2​(1−τ)=τ21−τ.\sum_{i\leq k}\frac{(\hat{p}_{i}-p_{i})^{2}}{p_{i}}=\Bigl(\frac{\tau}{1-\tau}\Bigr)^{2}\sum_{i\leq k}p_{i}=\Bigl(\frac{\tau}{1-\tau}\Bigr)^{2}(1-\tau)=\frac{\tau^{2}}{1-\tau}.

For i>ki>k, p^i=0\hat{p}_{i}=0, so

∑i>k(p^i−pi)2pi=∑i>kpi=τ.\sum_{i>k}\frac{(\hat{p}_{i}-p_{i})^{2}}{p_{i}}=\sum_{i>k}p_{i}=\tau.

Therefore

Dχ2(P^∥P)=τ21−τ+τ=τ1−τ.D_{\chi^{2}}(\hat{P}\|P)=\frac{\tau^{2}}{1-\tau}+\tau=\frac{\tau}{1-\tau}.

Combining the two displays gives

‖Attn⁡(q,K,V)−Attnk⁡(q,K,V)‖2=τ​‖μtail−μhead‖2≤τ1−τ​VarP⁡(V)=Dχ2(P^∥P)​VarP⁡(V),\bigl\|\operatorname{Attn}(q,K,V)-\operatorname{Attn}_{k}(q,K,V)\bigr\|_{2}=\tau\,\|\mu_{\mathrm{tail}}-\mu_{\mathrm{head}}\|_{2}\;\leq\;\sqrt{\frac{\tau}{1-\tau}}\,\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_{P}(V)}=\sqrt{D_{\chi^{2}}(\hat{P}\|P)}\,\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_{P}(V)},

as claimed. ∎

Corollary A.9 (Centered KL–variance bound).

Using the Top-kk identity KL(P^∥P)=−log(1−τ)\operatorname{KL}(\hat{P}\|P)=-\log(1-\tau), one has

‖Attn⁡(q,K,V)−Attnk⁡(q,K,V)‖2≤eKL(P^∥P)−1​VarP⁡(V).\bigl\|\operatorname{Attn}(q,K,V)-\operatorname{Attn}_{k}(q,K,V)\bigr\|_{2}\;\leq\;\sqrt{e^{\operatorname{KL}(\hat{P}\|P)}-1}\;\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_{P}(V)}.
Proof.

For any distributions P,P^P,\hat{P}, Dχ2(P^∥P)≤eKL(P^∥P)−1D_{\chi^{2}}(\hat{P}\|P)\leq e^{\operatorname{KL}(\hat{P}\|P)}-1. Combining this inequality with Proposition A.8 yields the desired bound. ∎

Theorem A.10 (Best available certificate).

Let C≥maxi⁡‖vi‖2C\geq\max_{i}\|v_{i}\|_{2}. Then, for Top-kk truncation,

‖Attn⁡(q,K,V)−Attnk⁡(q,K,V)‖2≤min⁡{τ​diamH,T,Dχ2(P^∥P)​VarP⁡(V), 2​C​τ}.\bigl\|\operatorname{Attn}(q,K,V)-\operatorname{Attn}_{k}(q,K,V)\bigr\|_{2}\;\leq\;\min\Bigl\{\tau\,\mathrm{diam}_{H,T},\;\sqrt{D_{\chi^{2}}(\hat{P}\|P)}\,\sqrt{\operatorname{Var}_{P}(V)},\;2C\,\tau\Bigr\}.
Proof.

The first term τ​diamH,T\tau\,\mathrm{diam}_{H,T} is given by the head–tail diameter bound (Proposition 5.3). The second term follows from the centered χ2\chi^{2}–variance bound (Proposition A.8). Finally, Proposition  A.4 gives the bound 2​C​τ2C\tau. Taking the minimum of these three valid upper bounds gives the result. ∎

Appendix B Gaussian Model

Assume si∼𝒩⁡(μ,σ2)s_{i}\sim\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^{2}) i.i.d. Then by the Law of Large Numbers,

1L​∑j=1Lesj→eμ+σ2/2.\frac{1}{L}\sum_{j=1}^{L}e^{s_{j}}\to e^{\mu+\sigma^{2}/2}. (7)

Proof of relation (7): Let s1,s2,…s_{1},s_{2},\dots be i.i.d. 𝒩⁡(μ,σ2)\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^{2}) and set Xj≔esjX_{j}\coloneqq e^{s_{j}}. We first compute

𝔼⁡[X1]=𝔼⁡[es1]=12​π​σ​∫ℝexp⁡(x−(x−μ)22​σ2)​𝑑x.\mathbb{E}[X_{1}]=\mathbb{E}[e^{s_{1}}]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\exp\!\left(x-\frac{(x-\mu)^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\,dx.

We now carry out the completion of the square in detail. Expand the quadratic term:

x−(x−μ)22​σ2=x−x2−2​μ​x+μ22​σ2=−x22​σ2+(μσ2+1)​x−μ22​σ2.x-\frac{(x-\mu)^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}=x-\frac{x^{2}-2\mu x+\mu^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}=-\frac{x^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}+\left(\frac{\mu}{\sigma^{2}}+1\right)x-\frac{\mu^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}.

Group the x2x^{2} and xx terms and factor −12​σ2-\frac{1}{2\sigma^{2}}:

x−(x−μ)22​σ2=−12​σ2​(x2−2​(μ+σ2)​x+μ2).x-\frac{(x-\mu)^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}=-\frac{1}{2\sigma^{2}}\!\left(x^{2}-2(\mu+\sigma^{2})x+\mu^{2}\right).

Complete the square inside the brackets:

x2−2​(μ+σ2)​x+μ2=(x−(μ+σ2))2−((μ+σ2)2−μ2).x^{2}-2(\mu+\sigma^{2})x+\mu^{2}=\bigl(x-(\mu+\sigma^{2})\bigr)^{2}-\bigl((\mu+\sigma^{2})^{2}-\mu^{2}\bigr).

Compute the constant explicitly:

(μ+σ2)2−μ2=2​μ​σ2+σ4.(\mu+\sigma^{2})^{2}-\mu^{2}=2\mu\sigma^{2}+\sigma^{4}.

Therefore

x−(x−μ)22​σ2=−(x−(μ+σ2))22​σ2+μ+σ22.x-\frac{(x-\mu)^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}=-\frac{(x-(\mu+\sigma^{2}))^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}+\mu+\frac{\sigma^{2}}{2}.

Substituting this back into the integral gives

𝔼⁡[es1]=12​π​σ​∫ℝexp⁡(−(x−(μ+σ2))22​σ2)​𝑑x⋅eμ+σ2/2.\mathbb{E}[e^{s_{1}}]=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-(\mu+\sigma^{2}))^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\,dx\;\cdot\;e^{\mu+\sigma^{2}/2}.

Make the change of variables z=x−(μ+σ2)σz=\frac{x-(\mu+\sigma^{2})}{\sigma}, so d​x=σ​d​zdx=\sigma\,dz; then

12​π​σ∫ℝexp(−(x−(μ+σ2))22​σ2)dx=12​π∫ℝe−z2/2dz=1.\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\sigma}\int_{\mathbb{R}}\exp\!\left(-\frac{(x-(\mu+\sigma^{2}))^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\,dx=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}}\int_{\mathbb{R}}e^{-z^{2}/2}\,dz=1.

Hence

𝔼⁡[es1]=eμ+σ2/2.\mathbb{E}[e^{s_{1}}]=e^{\mu+\sigma^{2}/2}.

In particular 𝔼⁡[|X1|]<∞\mathbb{E}[|X_{1}|]<\infty, so by the Strong Law of Large Numbers,

1L​∑j=1Lesj=1L​∑j=1LXj→L→∞a.s.𝔼⁡[X1]=eμ+σ2/2,\frac{1}{L}\sum_{j=1}^{L}e^{s_{j}}=\frac{1}{L}\sum_{j=1}^{L}X_{j}\xrightarrow[L\to\infty]{\text{a.s.}}\mathbb{E}[X_{1}]=e^{\mu+\sigma^{2}/2},

which is exactly relation (7). ∎

For a threshold tt,

1L∑i:si>tesi⟶eμ+σ2/2Φc(t−μ−σ2σ).\frac{1}{L}\sum_{i:\,s_{i}>t}e^{s_{i}}\;\longrightarrow\;e^{\mu+\sigma^{2}/2}\;\Phi_{c}\!\left(\frac{t-\mu-\sigma^{2}}{\sigma}\right). (8)

Proof of relation (8). Fix t∈ℝt\in\mathbb{R} and let s1,s2,…s_{1},s_{2},\dots be i.i.d. 𝒩⁡(μ,σ2)\mathcal{N}(\mu,\sigma^{2}). Define the integrable i.i.d. variables

𝔼⁡[Y1]=∫t∞ex​φμ,σ​(x)​𝑑x=12​π​σ​∫t∞exp⁡(x−(x−μ)22​σ2)​𝑑x.\mathbb{E}[Y_{1}]=\int_{t}^{\infty}e^{x}\,\varphi_{\mu,\sigma}(x)\,\mathrm{d}x=\frac{1}{\sqrt{2\pi}\,\sigma}\int_{t}^{\infty}\exp\!\left(x-\frac{(x-\mu)^{2}}{2\sigma^{2}}\right)\,\mathrm{d}x.

relations (7)–(8) imply
